result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give all ten events a clear treatment and keep push for cancellations, the expired card and connection-risk delays. A is clearly stronger on the auto-rebook: its sample message says what changed and offers undo or change, while B only says the user should see the new itinerary. A also adds a cap on rebooking without asking, early card-expiry warnings and a status screen that replaces the nothing-happened pings. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give all ten events a treatment and keep interrupting pushes for cancellations, the card problem and delays that matter. B is stronger on the auto-rebook. Its sample message says what the agent changed and offers an undo window and a way to change it, while A only says the user should see the new itinerary. B also states the 'no news stays quiet' rule more clearly and offers controls grouped by kind, with problem alerts that can't be turned off.
